notes: These cells are unfilled both in the historical appendix and in Lasry et al. Table 2 / Lasry dissertation Table 6.2, not merely unknown to the 1918 analysts. Baseline fills remain separate hypotheses unless an independent constraint supports them.

An illustrative square in paper Figure 2 / dissertation Figure 6.2 places VF=6 and XA=5, opposite the baseline fill. It also prints N twice (AX and XG), contradicting the final key table. Treat the two digits as unresolved, rather than elevating the inconsistent illustrative figure to an established key.

prior_credit: J. Rives Childs source; published period key by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), with Lasry 2017 disclosure. Prior OCR and the accepted p162 C2 edition are preserved. Current source collation and explicitly priced edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is claimed.
limits: The p162 C1 fragment by itself fixes zero labels in the source-linked 312 frame: 195 missing prefix coordinates remain unassigned in the primary baseline. Its complete reading is conditional on the independently observed p166 prefix.

The overlap has 114 independently agreeing coordinates, 2 observed disagreements and 1 absent p166 coordinate. Filling that coordinate from p162 creates a copied agreement, not a 115th independent agreement.
The missing-coordinate location has two aliases, original 225 and 226, both within the short XVGD group. They have different unfilled raw positions but the same filled XXVGD ciphertext.
Source-only alignment establishes the best match within the declared one-missing-coordinate frame. It does not rule out all other error histories or prove every transmitted glyph.
Three lexical substitutions are in the shared p166 prefix. They are counted once at their observed origins; p162 supplies no independent check of those prefix repairs.
Two p166 C1 substitutions are supported by coordinates in the p162 fragment; their other pair coordinates still come from p166. They are not complete plaintext pairs independently observed in p162.
The earlier p162 C2 edition is a supporting witness only and is not counted as a fourth new physical record.

The literal wording MITTEILT, labels AKONACH18 and AKONACH17ROEM4, and all separators remain unchanged. No person, unit, exact military function, border or historical event is identified beyond the source language.
